TEVRA workflow

Source: vignettes/TEVRA.Rmd
TEVRA.Rmd
library(TEVRA)
library(SingleCellExperiment)

set.seed(0)

Load data

TEVRA accepts a SingleCellExperiment object. Communities of transcriptionally similar cells can be computed upstream of the TEVRA workflow using any preferred method e.g., miloR, metacell or supercell. If discrete communities have been defined, these should be stored as a column in colData(sce_object). If overlapping neighbourhoods were computed e.g., via miloR, these should be stored as a binary nhoods matrix.

data(tevra_example)
tevra_example

#> dim: 2000 3430 
#> metadata(1): graphs
#> assays(1): logcounts

#> colData names(18): orig.ident nCount_RNA ... CTaa_BCR_IGH CTaa_BCR_IGL
#> reducedDimNames(2): PCA UMAP
#> mainExpName: RNA

Create communities

TEVRA also provides create_communities(), a custom function for community detection. This operates via Leiden partitioning of a pre-computed shared-nearest-neighbour graph. The key parameters are:

  • resolution: determines the granularity of clustering
  • min_cells: informs the minimum number of cells per community. Cells belonging to communities with fewer cells are reassigned to the community occupied by the majority of the cell’s nearest neighbours

To establish communities of the desired size, different resolutions can be evaluated via test_resolution() and visualised via plot_resolution_results()

res_results <- test_resolution(tevra_example,
                               graph.name = "RNA_snn",
                               resolutions = c(0.5,1,2.5,5,10,20),
                               min_cells = 5)

Once the optimal resolution has been selected, communities can be generated via create_communities() and community sizes evaluated via plot_nhood_sizes()

communities <- create_communities(tevra_example,
                                  graph.name = "RNA_snn",
                                  resolution = 5,
                                  min_cells = 5,
                                  feature.col = "nFeature_RNA",
                                  count.col = "nCount_RNA")
#> [1] "Created 50 communities"
#> [1] "Mean cells per community: 68.6"

A neighbourhood-level UMAP can be generated via aggregating (mean or median) the consistuent cells’ individual UMAP coordinates per neighbourhood

sce_obj <- nhood_umap(sce_obj,
                      nhood_col = "community_id",
                      aggregate_fun = "median",
                      result_name   = "nhood_umap")
#> Neighbourhood UMAP centroids (median) for 50 neighbourhoods stored in metadata(object)[['nhood_umap']].

head(metadata(sce_obj)$nhood_umap)
#>   nhood nhood_size median_UMAP_1 median_UMAP_2

Neighbourhood level analysis

Once cells are aggregated into transcriptionally-defined neighbourhoods, these can be fed into TEVRA’s neighbourhood-level analysis functions.

Neighbourhood annotation

Each neighbourhood can be annotated according to the most common identity among its constituent cells. Specify one or more colData columns in annotation_cols. For each column, the most frequent value across the neighbourhood’s cells becomes the neighbourhood’s annotation, provided it accounts for a proportion of cells above the defined threshold.

sce_obj <- nhood_annotation(object = sce_obj,
                            annotation_cols = "Bcelltype",
                            nhood_col = "community_id",
                            threshold = 0.5,
                            result_name = "nhood_annotation")
#> Annotation column 'Bcelltype':
#>   49 / 50 neighbourhoods assigned a dominant identity (threshold = 0.50).
#>   1 / 50 neighbourhoods labelled 'mixed' (no identity exceeded threshold = 0.50).
#>   Dominant identity breakdown:
#>     Follicular 1: 12 neighbourhood(s)
#>     Follicular 2: 11 neighbourhood(s)
#>     Follicular 3: 8 neighbourhood(s)
#>     Transitional: 7 neighbourhood(s)
#>     Follicular 4: 5 neighbourhood(s)
#>     B1: 2 neighbourhood(s)
#>     MZ: 2 neighbourhood(s)
#>     Follicular 5: 1 neighbourhood(s)
#>     Plasma: 1 neighbourhood(s)
#> Stored annotation results (50 neighbourhoods x 1 annotation column(s)) in metadata(object)[['nhood_annotation']].

head(metadata(sce_obj)$nhood_annotation)
#>   nhood nhood_size    Bcelltype Bcelltype_dominant_prop

To investigatethe proportion of cells per neighbourhood with each identity without assigning a neighbourhood annotation, run nhood_annotation_props()

Neighbourhood diversity

The clonal repertoire of each neighbourhood is summarised using nhood_diversity(), selecting the specific diversity metrics desired from:

  • shannon:
  • norm.entropy
  • inv.simpson
  • gini.simpson
  • chao1
  • ace
  • gini
  • standardised_n_clones

If clones have not been defined, the raw cdr3 sequence is used as a surrogate, although this is not recommended for B cells due to the potential for significant sequence modification within clones via somatic hypermutation. Metrics are not computed for neighbourhoods with less than min_n_contigs as diversity estimates are unstable at low sample sizes. Rarefaction or coverage- based standardisation is recommended due to the sensitivity of diversity estimates to sampling depth

sce_obj <- nhood_diversity(sce_obj,
                           nhood_col = "community_id",
                           clone_id_col = "CTstrict_BCR",
                           cdr3_col = "CTnt_BCR",
                           min_n_contigs = 10,
                           metrics = c("shannon", "inv.simpson", "gini.simpson", "chao1"),
                           downsample_method = "rarefaction",
                           n_boots = 100,
                           feature_scale = FALSE,
                           result_name = "nhood_diversity")
#> Warning in nhood_diversity(sce_obj, nhood_col = "community_id", clone_id_col =
#> "CTstrict_BCR", : Rarefaction is not compatible with chao1 or ace estimators.

Neighbourhood cdr3 convergence

The similarity of the CDR3 amino acid sequences of different clones is computed using nhood_cdr3_convergence(). This is computed for both heavy and light chain CDR3 sequences when chain = “both”.

Pairwise distances are computed via pwalign’s stringDist() function across all unique (or representative when receptor_type = “BCR”) CDR3 amino acid sequences per neighbourhood exceeding min_n_contigs and optionally min_clones. These are either traditional Levenshtein distances or calculated using BLOSUM-weighted substitution scores. Raw alignment distances are then normalised to [0,1] by dividing by the length of the longer sequence in each pair. To control for variation in clone number across neighbourhoods, distance matrices may be downsampled over n_boots iterations.

Pairwise distances matrices are summarised per neighbourhood as a global convergence score (mean or median pairwise distance across all representative CDR3 sequences), or a local convergence score (mean distance of each CDR3 sequence to its k nearest neighbours, averaged across representatives). Finally, all distance-based metrics are converted to convergence scores via \(1 - distance\).

sce_obj <- nhood_cdr3_convergence(object = sce_obj,
                                  nhood_col ="community_id",
                                  receptor_type = "BCR",
                                  chain = "both",
                                  aa_col = c(VDJ = "CTaa_BCR_IGH", VJ = "CTaa_BCR_IGL"),
                                  clone_id_col = "CTstrict_BCR",
                                  min_n_contigs = 10,
                                  min_clones = NULL,
                                  distance_method = "levenshtein", 
                                  summary_metric = "converge_score",
                                  downsample = TRUE,
                                  n_boots = 100,
                                  BPPARAM = BiocParallel::SerialParam(),
                                  result_name = "nhood_cdr3_convergence") 
#> Extracting neighbourhood membership...

To investigate the raw convergence matrices without neighbourhood-level summarisation, run nhood_cdr3_convergence_matrices().

Merge neighbourhood-level analysis

merge_nhood_results() easily aggregates all neighbourhood-level analyses into a single dataframe for plotting and visualisation purposes.

sce_obj <- merge_nhood_results(object = sce_obj,
                               dataframe_names = c("nhood_umap", "nhood_annotation", 
                                "nhood_diversity", "nhood_cdr3_convergence"),
                               merge_key = "nhood",
                               size_col = "nhood_size",
                               verbose = TRUE,
                               result_name = "merged_nhood_analysis")
#> ======================================================================
#> Merging Neighbourhood Analysis Results
#> ======================================================================
#> Checking available data (4 requested):
#>   nhood_umap: ✓ Found

#>   nhood_diversity: ✓ Found

Plot

TEVRA offers a number of visualisation functions. Each neighbourhood is visualised as a point.

Neighbourhood UMAP 

cell_umap_coords <- as.data.frame(reducedDims(sce_obj)$UMAP)
summary(row.names(cell_umap_coords) == row.names(colData(sce_obj)))
#>    Mode    TRUE 
#> logical    3430
cell_umap_coords$community_id <- colData(sce_obj)$community_id

plot_nhood_umap(metadata(sce_obj)$merged_nhood_analysis,
                nhood_col = "nhood",
                x_col = "median_UMAP_1",
                y_col = "median_UMAP_2",
                fill_by = "Bcelltype",
                show_cells = T,
                cell_umap_coords = cell_umap_coords,
                cell_x_col = "umap_1",
                cell_y_col = "umap_2",
                cell_colour_by = "nhood",
                cell_nhood_col = "community_id")

Capture efficiency

Visualises the efficiency of contig capture per neighbourhood. Follows nhood_diversity()

plot_capture_efficiency(nhood_diversity_df = metadata(sce_obj)$merged_nhood_analysis, 
                        group_by = "Bcelltype") 
#> $capture_rate

#> 
#> $count_vs_size
#> `geom_smooth()` using formula = 'y ~ x'

Beeswarm 

plot_nhood_beeswarm(metadata(sce_obj)$merged_nhood_analysis,
                    plot_cols = c("clone_per_contig" , "inv.simpson_diversity"),
                    reliability_col = "diversity_reliable",
                    group_by = "Bcelltype",
                    summary_metric = "group_median",
                    colour_by = "Bcelltype",
                    size_by = "nhood_size")
#> Orientation inferred to be along y-axis; override with
#> `position_quasirandom(orientation = 'x')`

Scatter plot 

plot_nhood_scatter(metadata(sce_obj)$merged_nhood_analysis,
                   x_col = "inv.simpson_diversity",
                   y_col = "CDR3_converge_score_VDJ",
                   x_reliability_col = "diversity_reliable",
                   y_reliability_col = "VDJ_converge_score_reliable",
                   colour_by = "Bcelltype",
                   size_by = "nhood_size")
